study_identification.title: Individualized cortical thickness asymmetry in Autism Spectrum Disorders and Schizophrenia

study_characteristics.study_objective: To investigate the degree of abnormal cortical thickness asymmetry at the individual level in Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD) and schizophrenia (SZ) using normative modeling.

dataset_name.answer: ABIDE-I, ABIDE-II, BGS, COBRE, Utrecht, AOMIC-ID1000, AOMIC-PIOP1, AOMIC-PIOP2, CAMCAN, DLBS, IXI, NARRATIVES, SALD, OASIS, ROCKLAND, MITASD, WASHASD, MADRID-ASD

quality_checking_detail.answer: Initially, only highest quality images from ABIDE were included. Then, a weighted overall image quality rating (IQR) from the Computational Anatomy Toolbox was used to exclude images with an IQR > 2.8 (682 images excluded). Finally, the Freesurfer Euler number was used to remove images with a within-dataset centered Euler number > 10 (5 images excluded).

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Bayesian Linear Regression with scanner as a covariate. Linear support vector classifiers were used to assess residual site effects, with mean balanced accuracy near chance level (50%) indicating minimal influence.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The model explicitly includes age, sex, Euler number (image quality), and scanner as covariates to account for their effects on the asymmetry index. This directly addresses nuisance variables.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: Subsequently, we used Bayesian Linear Regression (Fraza et al., 2021). The training set consisted of 4904 healthy individuals (54.85% female, age range: 6-95 years) which established a normative range for AI, considering an individual’s age, sex, Euler number, and scanner.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The study employed a ten-fold cross-validation approach on the training cohort to evaluate the generalization of the model.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: To evaluate the generalization of our model, we employed a ten-fold cross-validation approach on the training cohort. Specifically, we divided the training cohort into ten separate folds. In each fold, we trained BLR models using 90% of the participants as training data, while including age, sex, Euler number, and scanner as covariates, reserving the remaining 10% for assessing generalization performance.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study used a held-out test set of healthy controls (HCtest) to assess the model's performance on unseen data from the same domain.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: For each of the datasets exclusively comprising healthy controls 90% of individuals went into the training set and 10% into the test set (HCtest ) using the createDataPartition function from the caret R package.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study does not appear to validate the model on a dataset from a different domain (e.g., a completely independent cohort from different studies not included in the training/test split).
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: The paper does not mention any external validation on a different domain dataset.

clinical_dataset.answer: ABIDE-I, ABIDE-II, BGS, COBRE, Utrecht, MITASD, WASHASD, MADRID-ASD

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Permuted chi-square tests, Welch t-tests, Mann-Whitney U test, t-SNE with k-medoid clustering.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Variation in regional asymmetry of cortical thickness in individuals with ASD falls within the normal inter-individual variation, and extreme deviance from the norm in SZ appeared nearly equal to that in healthy controls.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Whole brain and regional supra- and infra-normal deviations of asymmetry of cortical thickness are present in similar proportions in individuals with ASD, SZ and healthy individuals. For individuals with SZ there was one region in the superior temporal cortex where individuals with SZ had a higher proportion of supra-normal z-scores compared to healthy individuals, with very low effect sizes. The multivariate results showed no relationship between the deviance of inter-regional pattern of cortical thickness asymmetry and diagnosis.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The study acknowledges limitations such as the need for larger and more heterogeneous datasets, incomplete deep phenotyping (handedness, IQ, symptomatology), and the focus on cortical thickness as opposed to other size or shape properties.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The results cast doubts on asymmetry of cortical thickness as a potential biomarker for ASD and SZ.

general_notes.general_notes: Full list of datasets: ABIDE-I NYU, ABIDE-I USM, ABIDE-II GU, ABIDE-II OHSU, MITASD, WASHASD, MADRID-ASD, BGS, COBRE, UTRECHT, AOMIC-ID1000, AOMIC-PIOP1, AOMIC-PIOP2, CAMCAN, DLBS, IXI, NARRATIVES, SALD, OASIS, ROCKLAND.
